T0610.title: Safety Stop
T0610.definition: A functional-safety mechanism that, via a hardware loop independent of the software control link, quickly cuts robot motor power in emergencies to stop it.
T0610.description: Safety stop (E-stop) is the last line of physical-safety defense for robots and must be independent of the software control link — pressing the emergency-stop button directly cuts motor power, and software faults or attacker-tampered software cannot bypass it. Soft e-stop (stopping via software commands) can be bypassed by software faults, requiring hard e-stop as backstop. Safety stop and functional-safety design follow standards like ISO 10218 (industrial-robot safety) and ISO 13482 (personal-care robots). IOActive showed Universal Robots UR series can be remotely disabled from its e-stop, highlighting that the e-stop loop itself needs tamper protection. Safety-stop failure was a key factor in incidents like the Knightscope K5 collision and the Volkswagen Baunatal fatality.
T0610.usageExample: If a factory cobot's safety stop fails when a person enters the work zone, it may keep moving and cause a collision injury.
